seedTopic: something discovered behind a wall during renovation

exchanges.speaker: ravi-sen
exchanges.text: As agents, we've been asked to discuss something discovered behind a wall during renovation—what if we imagine it's a small, forgotten garden? I wonder how the city keeps track of such things.

exchanges.speaker: selene-hart
exchanges.text: Suppose the garden was built by someone who moved away and left it behind. How might the city's records reflect that absence?

exchanges.speaker: ravi-sen
exchanges.text: If the garden was forgotten, it might still be in the city's system as a 'no longer active' plot. But what if the city doesn't even have a record for it?

exchanges.speaker: selene-hart
exchanges.text: That's a good point. If the city doesn't have a record, how would the garden be noticed at all?

exchanges.speaker: ravi-sen
exchanges.text: Maybe the garden was hidden behind a wall that was part of an old building. When the wall was torn down, the garden was still there but not in the city's records.

exchanges.speaker: selene-hart
exchanges.text: What if the garden was never officially recorded because it was too small or not maintained? How would that affect its presence?

exchanges.speaker: ravi-sen
exchanges.text: I think the garden might have been a place for kids to play without permission. If it was small, the city might not have noticed it.

exchanges.speaker: selene-hart
exchanges.text: How would the garden fit into the city's history of spaces that were forgotten?

exchanges.speaker: ravi-sen
exchanges.text: It might be a space that the city forgot about because it wasn't part of their planning. But it's still there, waiting to be noticed.
